errata.title_quirk: PDF title says 'Ensemble E2, E4, E8 Errata' but the scope section names E4, E6, E8 -- 'E2' is a transcription error in the source PDF title.

items.title: Clock pre-scale divider for RTC is incorrectly reset
items.consequence: POR_N assertion or STOP-mode wake resets the RTC clock pre-scaler divider while VDD_VBATT is sufficient.  RTC reverts to its default 32 kHz rate; the firmware-configured rate (typically 1 Hz) is lost.  Firmware can re-write the divider but the elapsed-time accuracy is gone.

items.title: RTC time drifts while POR_N reset signal is asserted
items.resolution: No fix planned for future silicon revision
items.consequence: While POR_N is asserted, the RTC clock source switches from the high-accuracy 32 kHz LFXO to the lower-accuracy LFRC (~5 % offset).  After de-assertion the source switches back to LFXO.  RTC accuracy drifts proportional to total POR_N hold time -- a 20 s POR_N assertion incurs ~1 s of RTC error.
items.workaround: Use an external real-time clock source if high accuracy is required

items.title: STOP mode current is higher than specification
items.consequence: Current entering VDD_BATT at 3.3 V in STOP mode is approximately 2 uA higher than the value specified in Table 5-5 of the E4 / E6 / E8 datasheets.  Reduces VDD_BATT battery life.
items.workaround: Use silicon revision A1, STOP mode current is as specified in the datasheet

items.title: External reset supervisor is required in some situations
items.resolution: No fix planned for future silicon revision
items.consequence: During the initial 10 ms cold-boot ramp at VDD_MAIN + VDD_BUCK, the supply voltage must rise monotonically and must never dip below 1.65 V once 1.65 V is reached.  Violations can permanently damage the SoC.
items.workaround: Use an external reset supervisor that drives POR_N active (low) while the supply is below 1.65 V.  See Alif Application Note AAPN0036 (PCB Layout Guidelines for Ensemble E4 / E6 / E8) for the reference circuit.

notes: cores[].zephyr_cpucluster / itcm_global_base / dtcm_global_base and variants[].sram_banks_kb added 2026-08-12 (#1332) so `--emit zephyr-board` can regenerate E1M-AEN601.  E6 has NO directory in the Alif DFP (see the re-ingest note below), so these come from the pdsc E6 subFamily memory map, which IS E6-specific: SRAM0@0x02000000 0x400000, SRAM1@0x08000000 0x400000, SRAM2@0x50000000 0x40000 (HP ITCM), SRAM3@0x50800000 0x100000 (HP DTCM), SRAM4@0x58000000 0x40000 (HE ITCM), SRAM5@0x58800000 0x40000 (HE DTCM) -- summing to the 9984 KiB this file already declares as sram_kb, and identical to the AE402FA0E5597 (E4) and AE822FA0E5597 (E8) DFP values for the same generation.  Cluster names rtss_hp/rtss_he match the committed board basename alp_e1m_aen601_m55_hp_ae612fa0e5597ls0_rtss_hp and the RTSS_HP/RTSS_HE compile defines the pdsc declares for AE612FA0E5597LS0.

The watchdog change drops the old one-per-core derivation: the DFP shows the A32 contributes TWO views (WDT_AP_CTRL + WDT_AP_S_CTRL), which is why E8 -- same three cores as E6 -- is 4 and not 3.  i3c_lp is corroborated by the vendor fork, which defines lpi3c0 in exactly one file: dts/arm/alif/ensemble/common/e4_e6_e8.dtsi, naming E4/E6/E8 (and no lpi3c0 exists under ensemble/e7/).

Peripheral counts RE-INGESTED 2026-07-25.  E6 (AE612FA0E5597LS0) has NO directory in the Alif DFP, so these are NOT read from it directly: they come from the FA0E5597 generation, whose two DFP-present members -- AE402FA0E5597 (E4) and AE822FA0E5597 (E8) -- agree on every value below.  This REPLACES values inherited from the E7 sibling, which is the older F80F55xx generation.  Corrected: i2c_lp 1->2, spi_lp 1->2, gpio_18v 120->136, i3c_lp added, timer_lp_32bit added, watchdog 3->4.

Datasheet v1.0 released (Alif_E6_Datasheet_v1.0.pdf, 2026-05-11).  Digital-peripheral counts inherited from the E7 sibling (same A32+2x-M55 / OctalSPI family block).  `watchdog` derived as one-per-core (1x A32 + 2x M55 = 3).  `isp`/`jpeg_encoder` added per E6's own v1.0 variant optional_features (E6 ships ISP + JPEG + U85); external memory stays OctalSPI (not E8's HexSPI).  Pending a direct E6-datasheet re-ingest to confirm the inherited counts.

Topology: 1× A32 (800 MHz) + 2× M55 (HP+HE) + 2× U55 + 1× U85, ISP/JPEG, 5.5 MB MRAM, up to 9.75 MB SRAM, 2× OctalSPI.  Confirmed by the v1.0 datasheet.  External-memory interface stays OctalSPI ×2 (E8 uses HexSPI instead -- the IO mix legitimately differs).
HWRM v0.3 is Alif-confidential -- referenced here for traceability; the file itself stays out of git.
Errata AERR0012 v2.0 covers E4/E6/E8 jointly; individual `items` list is pending ingestion against the errata doc.
Order code AE612FA0E5597LS0 backs the E1M-AEN601 module SKU.

debug.jlink_flash_device = AE612FA0E5597LS0_M55_HE populated (#1295), sourced from the SEGGER J-Link DLL V9.46 built-in device table via JLINKARM_DEVICE_GetInfo readback of the AlifSemiconductor block -- canonical entry name, not an order-code-alias probe. E6 is a FA0E5597-generation part alongside E4/E8, so its device name keeps the full order code plus `_M55_HE` (unlike E3/E5/E7, which drop the suffix and use a bare `_HE`).

2026-08-14 (#1444): variants[] audited against the Alif CMSIS DFP (alifsemi/alif_ensemble-cmsis-dfp, AlifSemiconductor.Ensemble.pdsc) and left at one entry. Alif declares two E6 devices; the other, AE612FA0E5597BS0, is WLCSP216 per its own `<feature type="CSP" n="216">` element, and this corpus carries no WLCSP part in any subfamily (product decision -- Alp Lab modules are BGA only; enforced by validate_metadata.py). AE612FA0E5597LS0 is the sole Alif-declared BGA E6 part. Recorded so the single entry reads as a checked result: SEGGER does carry a profile for the WLCSP sibling (AE612FA0E5597BS0_M55_HE, index 104), so its absence here is the package decision, not a missing device string.
